title: Interactive Grid playground
learningObjectives: Explain interactive grid playground and use CSS Grid to create responsive two-dimensional layouts.

understand.concept: A Grid playground exposes controls for columns, rows, gap, track sizing, item placement, and named areas. The preview should update from a single source of state and show the generated CSS declarations.
understand.whyItMatters: A useful lab separates container-level controls from item placement controls, supports keyboard interaction, and offers responsive testing. It should make implicit tracks visible rather than hiding unexpected layout behaviour.
understand.analogy: A grid playground is a floor-plan workbench: change the track plan and observe how the items occupy the spaces.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; CSS Grid follows formal track sizing, placement, and alignment algorithms.

explain.narrative: This starter displays a two-column grid with equal flexible tracks and a gap. Interactive controls are the build challenge.

examples.explanation: This starter displays a two-column grid with equal flexible tracks and a gap. Interactive controls are the build challenge.
examples.expectedOutput: A rendered CSS Grid example demonstrating the topic.

practise.guidedTask: Add controls for column count, gap, and a track sizing preset. Update the preview and display the matching CSS. Include a reset action.
practise.independentTask: Build a responsive card or dashboard layout using this concept. Test long labels and narrow viewports.
hints: Inspect grid tracks with browser developer tools.
Check implicit tracks and minimum sizing.
Keep DOM and keyboard reading order logical.

questions.prompt: Which controls are core container-level settings in a basic Grid playground?
questions.explanation: Grid track definitions and gaps configure the grid container.

questions.prompt: What should a responsive Grid layout preserve?
options: Readable content and logical DOM order
A fixed number of columns at every width
Visual placement regardless of keyboard order
questions.answer: Readable content and logical DOM order
questions.explanation: Responsive layout should adapt while preserving access and meaningful reading order.
